name: Daal Chawal
description: Comforting Pakistani lentils with a fragrant garlic-cumin tarka, served with fluffy basmati rice.
ingredients: 1 cup moong or masoor lentils, rinsed
2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20–30 minutes
method: Put the rinsed lentils in a pot with turmeric, salt and about 3 cups water. Bring to a boil, then simmer until tender, adding a little hot water if needed.
Add the chopped tomato to the tender lentils and simmer until it softens. Adjust the daal to your preferred consistency.
For the rice, bring plenty of salted water to a boil, add the drained soaked basmati and cook until tender but the grains remain intact. Drain well and rest covered for a few minutes.
Heat ghee or oil in a small pan. Fry cumin seeds, sliced garlic and onion until fragrant and golden, then add the red chili powder briefly without burning it.
Carefully pour the hot tarka over the daal and stir lightly.
Taste for salt and serve the hot daal with rice, achaar and salad.
tips: Lentils thicken as they stand, so keep a little hot water available to adjust consistency.
Do not burn the garlic or chili in the tarka; both can turn bitter.
storage: Cool rice and daal promptly and refrigerate separately in covered containers for up to 2 days. Reheat until steaming hot throughout.
